Import an SBML Model

Source: R/SBMLinterface.R
importSbml.Rd

Reads an SBML Level 3 file. Requires rjson and reticulate, which provides a Python with python-libsbml; set the environment variable DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON to the path of a Python interpreter to use that one instead. Kinetic laws are divided by the volume of their compartment.

Usage

importSbml(modelpath, keep = NULL)

Arguments

modelpath

Path to the SBML file.

keep

Parameter ids that keep their own symbol although the SBML sets them by an <initialAssignment>; a constant assignment becomes their default value. Any other initial assignment is substituted into the rates, initial values and observables. Default NULL.

Value

A list with components

reactions

The model as an eqnlist.

pars

Named numeric, the parameter values.

inits

Named character, the initial value of each state.

observables

Named list of observable formulas, possibly empty.

assignmentRules

Named list of the formulas of the assignment rules and of the parameter initial assignments that keep does not name, already substituted into rates, initial values and observables.

events

An eventlist or NULL, including the rescaling of states when an event changes a compartment volume.

eventsSource

An eventlist or NULL, the event assignments of the SBML file only.

renamed

Named character, the new ids of SBML ids that are no valid R or C++ names, named by the old ids.

See also

exportSbml(), importPEtab()

Examples

f <- addReaction(eqnlist(), from = "A", to = "B", rate = "k1*A")
f <- addReaction(f, from = "B", to = "", rate = "k2*B")
file <- file.path(tempdir(), "model.xml")
exportSbml(f, parameters = c(k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.1), inits = c(A = 1, B = 0),
           filepath = file)
model <- importSbml(file)
model$reactions
#> 
#>   Check Educt -> Product       Rate Description
#> 1           A ->       B 1 * k1 * A           1
#> 2           B ->         1 * k2 * B           2
model$pars
#>          k1          k2 defaultComp 
#>         0.5         0.1         1.0
